fundamentals.name: Roundhill Memory ETF
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: The fund will generally seek to invest primarily in the equity securities of “Memory Companies,” but may also seek exposure to Memory Companies through derivative instruments, such as swap agreements and forward contracts. Under normal circumstances, it invests at least 80% of its net assets (plus borrowings for investment purposes) in equity securities or instruments (i.e., swap agreements or forward contracts) that provide exposure to Memory Companies. The fund is non-diversified.

Memory chip prices are volatile and critical to the ETF's performance.
Recent AI sell-off has negatively impacted related stocks.

news.paragraph: DRAM, the Roundhill Memory ETF, experienced a significant 15% drop following a guidance miss, with its CEO recently highlighting how AI demand is reshaping valuation methods for memory stocks. The ETF's performance is closely tied to memory chip prices, which are expected to be a key factor before year-end. Recent weakness in AI-linked stocks has also impacted major memory players like Samsung and SK Hynix, contributing to DRAM's recent downturn.
